subject.title: Agent loop allows simulated tool calls instead of enforcing real tool invocation

question: What should OpenClaw do by default when an agent turn emits tool-call-shaped assistant text instead of structured toolCall/toolUse content?
rationale: Current source combines warning-only diagnostics, limited compatibility promotion, and scoped Gateway HTTP enforcement; choosing stricter rejection, forced retry, or default promotion changes both the security boundary and local-model compatibility contract.

options.title: Define Bounded Enforcement
options.body: Choose the exact warning, suppression, promotion, retry, or fail-closed contract and implement it with focused agent-loop, provider, Gateway, and docs coverage.

options.title: Keep Warning-Only Compatibility
options.body: Document fake tool-call text as provider/model incompatibility and accept that it can still reach transcripts or visible replies without a real tool call.

options.title: Split Broader Claim Checks
options.body: Limit this issue to syntactic fake tool-call text and track natural-language success claims under broader response-gate or claim-ledger work.

recommendation.title: Define Bounded Enforcement
recommendation.body: Choose the exact warning, suppression, promotion, retry, or fail-closed contract and implement it with focused agent-loop, provider, Gateway, and docs coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans core agent-runtime security defaults and local-model compatibility, and recent history routes the relevant agent runtime and diagnostic seams through steipete's work.
